Dear Reena Apa,
It's been one of those weeks. Ammi has a new line: 'You should be married by twenty-three, like your sister.' It comes with breakfast, with the news, even with the laundry. And the other one: 'You should do B.Ed. Design is not a proper career for a girl from our family.'
The thing is, I know she means it lovingly. She stays up to heat my dinner when studio runs late. She keeps my old drawings in her cupboard. That's why it's so hard. If she were only strict, I could be angry. Instead I feel grateful and squashed at the same time.
I don't want to fight her. I want to keep having chai with her in the evenings. But I also want to finish this design course, and marry when it feels right.
How did you tell her what you wanted without hurting her?
Your little sister,
Sabina
